findings.location: .claude/scripts/tests/release-claims-check.test.sh:226-230 (the comment 'Non-vacuity for the three above' and the assertion it introduces)
findings.evidence: MEASURED, five independent cases, and it answers the operator's question (4) with the worst available answer: the assertion NEVER RUNS --help. Its command substitution is `tail -n +2 "$CHECKER" | awk '/^#/ { last = NR + 1; next } /^$/ { next } { exit } END { exit (last > 0 ? 0 : 1) }'` — it reads the checker's SOURCE, not its output; `$out_help` is not referenced; `last` is assigned the header's last line number and then DISCARDED, only `last > 0` is tested. (A) shipped build: rc 0, PASS. (B) the round-7 build reconstructed by reverting the arm to `sed -n '1,60p'` — the exact regression the assertion is named for — rc 0, STILL PASSES. (C) a build whose help printer is replaced by `:` so `--help` emits ZERO BYTES: rc 0, STILL PASSES, i.e. the shipped test prints `PASS: the header's last comment line is inside the rendered help` while there is no rendered help at all. (D) a 4-line script with a one-line header: PASS. (E) the ONLY input that returns 1 is a script with no header comment whatsoever. Then the load-bearing measurement: I swept the truncation window from 1,60p to 1,71p and ran all seven section-7 assertions against each build. 1,60p -> 4 fail (detected). 1,66p -> 1 fails (detected). 1,67p, 1,68p, 1,70p, 1,71p -> ALL SEVEN GREEN. So there is a five-line-wide truncation band (header source lines 68-72, the entire `BOTH CHECKERS TAKE A FILE` paragraph) that section 7 does not detect at all, and the one assertion written to close exactly that gap is green throughout it. The four content assertions are pinned strings whose highest position is `Exit:` at :67; by construction they can only see truncation that reaches :67, never growth past it — which is the R7-F1 failure mode restated. Proved the fix flips: computing the last header line's TEXT and asserting it is in $out_help gives shipped=PASS, reverted=FAIL, zero-help=FAIL.
findings.description: This is the documented FALSE-PAIR shape, verbatim: .claude/tests/README.md:560 makes leg 4 'at least one leg observes the shipped artifact RUNNING' the discriminator, and :570-572 records that 'Every FALSE-PAIR row compares bytes in markdown, in JSON, or in a script's COMMENT TEXT. Not one document check reached leg 4.' This assertion compares a script's comment text and does not execute the artifact. CLAUDE.md states the same rule as a hard gate ('if you are adding a new CHECK of any kind ... it does not ship without a negative control, and at least one leg must observe the shipped artifact RUNNING'). THE SHIPPED CLAIMS THAT ARE FALSE, which is why this is HIGH and not INFO: (a) ':226 Non-vacuity for the three above' — it supplies no non-vacuity for anything, proved by (B); (b) ':226-227 prove the header really does end after the exit contract' — it proves only that at least one header comment line exists, and would pass identically if the header ended BEFORE the exit contract; (c) ':227-228 so "renders to the end" is a claim about the whole file rather than about a window that happens to be wide enough today' — false, and measurably so: the 67..71 band above is precisely a window that happens to be wide enough today. The harm is the R6-F2 harm shape this round's own sequence already graded HIGH — an author who trusts the claim loses coverage on the defect class the artifact exists to catch. Concretely: the awk printer's own rationale sells itself as 'Self-adjusting means it cannot recur' (release-claims-check.sh:95), and this assertion is the only thing that could have verified self-adjustment; with it vacuous, the spec's protection against recurrence is pinned strings only. FIX (small, and it stays inside the operator's scope): replace the awk with `last_hdr=$(awk 'NR==1{next} /^#/{ l=$0; sub(/^# ?/,"",l); last=l; next } /^$/{next} {exit} END{print last}' "$CHECKER")` then `assert_contains "..." "$last_hdr" "$out_help"` — verified above to flip PASS/FAIL/FAIL across the three builds, and it drops the pipeline in R8-F4 as a side effect. IN FAIRNESS, and the operator should weigh it before applying the pre-committed revert: the assertion is REDUNDANT, the four content assertions genuinely do catch the R7-F1 regression (proved 4/5 below), and deleting lines 226-230 outright leaves section 7 correct and honest. The defect is confined to one assertion and its three-line comment.
findings.stop_rule_side: makes a SHIPPED CLAIM FALSE -> HIGH, blocking. The false claims are (a),(b),(c) above, all in the change set under review, all about what a shipped check verifies.

findings.evidence: MEASURED per-assertion, not in aggregate, which is what the operator asked for. I rebuilt the round-7 build independently (replace the -h|--help arm's awk with `sed -n '1,60p'`; cmp-proved the fixture differs from the source; bash -n clean) and grepped each asserted string in both renderings. new=1/old=0 for 'an additional file to check (repeatable)' (header :62), 'a surface that silently vanished' (:63), 'one-line JSON envelope' (:65) and 'Exit: 0 all surfaces agree' (:67) — all four genuinely DETECT the regression. new=1/old=1 for 'IT EXEMPTS THE WHOLE LINE' (:41) — it SURVIVES the regression it is grouped with, because :41 is comfortably inside the old 60-line window. '--help exits 0' also survives (the reverted build exits 0 too), though it is honestly named and is a contract assertion rather than a truncation control.
findings.description: The section rationale at :208-210 says the assertions 'name the LAST things in the header, so any future truncation fails here rather than in a reader's terminal.' Applied to the five content assertions that is a false universal: one of them names header line 41 of 72 — a middle thing — and it is green under the regression the paragraph is describing. The assertion's OWN name is honest ('--help carries the tally-xref line-granularity warning (R6-F2)') and it guards a real and different property: that the R6-F2 correction still reaches a reader. So the assertion should stay; the paragraph should stop claiming it as part of the truncation control. MEDIUM rather than HIGH because the operative half of the sentence is true — a truncation that reaches :67 does fail here — and the R6-F2 assertion's own label does not over-claim; only the grouping sentence does. Worth stating beside R8-F1: with that assertion excluded, the truncation control is four pinned strings whose highest position is :67, which is exactly the 67..71 blind band R8-F1 measures.
findings.stop_rule_side: a shipped claim that is false as a universal but true of four of its five subjects; graded MEDIUM, below the operator's HIGH bar, because the control it describes does exist and works.

findings.location: .claude/scripts/release-claims-check.sh:96-99 (the awk help printer) and :95 ('Self-adjusting means it cannot recur')
findings.evidence: MEASURED. The awk's continuation rules are `/^#/` and `/^$/`, both anchored with no leading-whitespace tolerance, so any header line that is whitespace-only or indented terminates the printer. Inserting a single line containing three spaces at header line 40 cuts --help from 72 lines to 38, drops 'Exit: 0 all surfaces agree' (grep -c 0) and still exits 0 — the identical silent-truncation signature as R7-F1. Inserting '  # indented note' at the same position does the same thing (38 lines, exit contract gone, rc 0). Neither shape exists in the shipped header today: an awk sweep of lines 1-80 for /^[[:space:]]+$/ returns none. Section 7 WOULD catch both (5/5 content assertions fail on each mutant), so the regression is gated, unlike R7-F1 which was ungated. The shipped stop point is exact: help output is 72 lines = source lines 2..73, terminating at :74 `set -uo pipefail`. Shebang, bare-'#' lines (:3 renders as a blank) and the blank line at :73 all behave as the operator asked about.
findings.description: The comment at :95 reads 'Self-adjusting means it cannot recur.' Under its own antecedent — the whole paragraph is about a MAGIC NUMBER drifting out of step with the header — that is TRUE, and I am not escalating it: number-drift genuinely cannot recur. As a bare universal over 'truncation' it is false, since a stray trailing space during a header reflow reproduces the exact R7-F1 symptom. LOW because the shipped header is clean, section 7 catches it, and the fix is one token in each rule: `/^[[:space:]]*#/` and `/^[[:space:]]*$/`. Offered as a v5.0.1 candidate for claude-workflow-plugin-8bbw alongside narrowing :95 to 'the fixed-count drift cannot recur'.
findings.stop_rule_side: makes a TRUE claim MORE PRECISE (the :95 wording) over a real but gated latent behaviour -> LOW / v5.0.1, not fix-now.

findings.location: .claude/scripts/tests/release-claims-check.test.sh:230 (`tail -n +2 "$CHECKER" | awk '... { exit } ...'` under the file-scope `set -uo pipefail` at :37)
findings.evidence: MEASURED. The awk exits at the first code line, so on a large enough input `tail` is SIGPIPEd and pipefail promotes the pipeline status to 141, which the assertion captures via `; echo $?` and compares against '0'. Reproduced in a standalone harness with the same `set -uo pipefail`: against the shipped 16,935-byte checker the pipeline returns 0 (tail finishes inside the 64KB pipe buffer before awk exits); against the same header followed by 2,124,196 bytes of code the pipeline returns 141 and the assertion would fail spuriously. The margin today is 16,935 of ~65,536 bytes.
findings.description: Latent, not live: the checker would have to grow roughly fourfold. Recorded because it is a fragility in a test whose failure mode would look like a real regression and send the next reviewer after the help printer. The R8-F1 replacement removes it incidentally — that form passes the file as an awk argument with no pipeline at all — so fixing F1 fixes this. If lines 226-230 are deleted instead, this disappears with them.
findings.stop_rule_side: neither arm: a latent harness fragility, nothing claimed false. Non-blocking; folds into whichever way R8-F1 is resolved.
